---
title: Fence termination fixture
---

Quarto closes a cell only on a fence whose backtick run is EXACTLY the opener's
(`breakQuartoMd`: `match(endCodeRegEx)[1].length === inCode`), and pandoc's
`markdown` treats a fence that never closes as prose rather than a code block.
So neither malformed shape below is a cell, and flagging either would be a false
positive (Session 179, measured firsthand vs 1.7.33).

The well-formed control comes FIRST and the run lengths ASCEND after it, both on
purpose: a bare closing run below an earlier opener would close it. Reordering
this file or renumbering the fences will change what it tests.

The control. Quarto really does validate this one, so it MUST be flagged.

```{r}
#| echo: maybe
1
```

A LONGER closer does not close a cell — CommonMark says it does, quarto does not.

````{r}
#| echo: maybe
2
`````

An UNTERMINATED cell is not a cell at all: quarto deletes the opening fence and
flushes the rest as markdown.

``````{r}
#| echo: maybe
3
